why_this_is_a_draft: 34 verified US leadership events at privately held employers, none of them enumerated from SEC EDGAR. They are NOT measurable as they stand and the file name carries `.draft` so that goldset.all_paths() skips it. Two things are missing. First, San Francisco and New York have no leadership rows at all, because the passes for those two metros ran out of web-search budget, so two of the four metro cells would be empty. Second, 30 of these 34 are company press releases, which would put one document type at 60% of a pooled set and trip US_REQUIRED_SHAPE['max_source_type_share']. Both are fixable by two more research passes and neither is fixable by editing this file.
the_enumerator_that_worked: Searching a press-release wire for the literal DATELINE text, for example 'DENVER, June' or 'SALT LAKE CITY, July', returns exactly the releases datelined in that city in that month and can be walked in date order. That is a genuine chronological enumerator over private employers, it is not one of our own feeds, and it is what to use for the San Francisco and New York passes. Its bias is that it only sees employers who pay a wire to distribute; pair it with metro business press people-on-the-move columns, which reach the rest.

sampling_by_cell.austin_leadership: SEC EDGAR was not used at any point. My WebSearch quota was already exhausted when this cell started, so I enumerated entirely through publishers' own on-site search and index pages, fetched directly. My primary enumerator was PR Newswire's own news search, which does phrase matching: I first walked the dense, low-noise phrase sets 'Austin-based' (120 results), 'headquartered in Austin' (255), 'Austin, Texas-based' (39) and the suburb phrases 'Round Rock, Texas' (55), 'Cedar Park, Texas' (15), 'Georgetown, Texas' (32), 'San Marcos, Texas' (24), 'Leander, Texas' (7) and 'Pflugerville' (17), listing every release each returned inside the window. I then walked the two broad sets 'Austin' (4,755 results) and 'Austin, Texas' (2,878) page by page in strict reverse-chronological order from the page covering 4 August 2026 back to the page covering 27 May 2026, so pages 2 through 9 of each covered 1 June to 31 July inclusive, and took every leadership headline in the order it appeared. Alongside the wires I ran on-site searches at UT Austin's newsroom, Texas State University's newsroom, the Austin Monitor and Community Impact, and tried the newsrooms of St. David's HealthCare and Southwestern University. Every row below was fetched and read individually to confirm company, person, role, headquarters city and year before it was recorded. What I had to drop: Business Wire and GlobeNewswire site search timed out on every attempt (60s) so those two wires are simply not represented, the Austin Business Journal and Austin Inno are not fetchable by this client at all, KXAN returned 403, and Southwestern University and St. David's returned empty shells. Genuine misses on the merits were Brazos Residential (Dallas HQ), Einride (Stockholm HQ), Venus Aerospace (Houston HQ) and several Austin releases whose subject was a VP, a science advisor or a strategic advisor rather than an executive-team role. Late July 2026 is visibly thinner than June in this metro, which is a real property of the window and not a sampling gap.
sampling_by_cell.rest_leadership_west: I did not touch EDGAR at all. My session's web-search budget was already exhausted before I began, so every enumerator had to be a page I could fetch directly and walk in order. I first tried regional enumerators (a Seattle tech outlet's monthly archives, an Arizona business outlet's people column, a San Diego daily's business section, a Las Vegas business section, an Oregon business magazine and a Boise news site) plus the newsrooms of nonprofit health systems (OHSU, Fred Hutch, Scripps); these mostly returned only current August content, and two returned 403, so they yielded nothing inside the window. I then walked a wire service's Personnel Announcements category listing chronologically backwards page by page from 11 August to 7 July, but its listing pages do not expose datelines, so metro filtering from headlines alone proved too lossy. What finally worked was searching the same wire on its dateline text (for example the literal string 'DENVER, June' or 'SALT LAKE CITY, July'), which returns exactly the releases datelined in that city that month; I ran that for each of my ten metros for both June and July and walked each result set in date order, taking every senior-executive event it gave me rather than picking. Portland and Sacramento returned no qualifying in-window leadership events and are absent for that reason, and I dropped several genuine finds for being VP-level rather than executive team, for sitting outside my metros, or for exceeding the three-per-metro cap. Every row below was verified by fetching the release itself and reading its dateline, and I quote what each page said.
sampling_by_cell.rest_leadership_east: I did not touch SEC EDGAR at any point. I started with the press pages of large privately held and nonprofit employers in my metros (health systems first: Henry Ford Health, UPMC, Cleveland Clinic, Vanderbilt University Medical Center), but those newsroom indexes are JavaScript-rendered and returned nothing for June-July 2026, and the trade and wire enumerator indexes I tried next (a hospital trade outlet's executive-moves section, a CEO trade magazine's moves category, the PR Newswire personnel list and the Business Wire personnel subject page) returned 403, 404 or timed out. My session's web-search budget was exhausted before I began, so my working enumerator became a set of date-bounded public news feeds restricted to 2026-06-01 through 2026-07-31, run metro-group by metro-group in this order: Boston; Cleveland/Pittsburgh/Columbus; Chicago; Philadelphia/Washington DC; Atlanta/Charlotte/Nashville; Dallas/Houston/Kansas City/St Louis. I walked each feed's returned items in the order given and kept every leadership event that fell in the window, in one of my metros, and at a privately held or nonprofit employer, resolving each candidate to its ORIGINAL publisher (the employer's own newsroom where it existed, otherwise a named local daily, public broadcaster or specialist outlet) and fetching that page before recording the row. I dropped the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation because the organization's own release page carries a 2019 date that contradicts the 2026 secondary report, and I lost several otherwise-good rows to publisher blocks (Grant Park Music Festival's own site, MLB.com, the Twin Cities daily) which I re-verified through a second named outlet where one existed. The Cleveland, Pittsburgh, Columbus, Detroit, Philadelphia, Miami, Charlotte, Raleigh-Durham, Kansas City and Dallas legs produced no row that cleared both the private-employer bar and the fetch-and-read bar, so the twelve are concentrated in Boston, Chicago, Nashville and St Louis.
